newsitem.title: USA: U S West Comms Q1 EPS surpass expectations.
newsitem.headline: U S West Comms Q1 EPS surpass expectations.

text.p: U S West Communications Group reported first quarter earnings several cents ahead of Wall Street expectations. The company cited, in part, successful marketing and tighter cost controls.
U S West's first quarter net earnings totalled $328 million, or $0.68 a share, up from $289 million, or $0.61 a share, a year earlier.
The First Call consensus estimate was $0.65 per share.
Revenues grew five percent to $2.59 billion, while operating expense growth slowed despite new investments, rising just four percent to $1.94 billion.

First quarter results included an $11 million adjustment associated with the sale of selected rural exchanges in Nebraska that cut earnings by $0.02 per share. Year-earlier results reflected charges of $39 million, or $0.08 per share, to cover a change in accounting.
The company said local service revenue grew 7.5 percent to $1.23 billion in the quarter, with almost half of the growth driven by sales of value-added features beyond basic access.
Local service revenues would have grown 8.9 percent but for a cut in cellular pricing mandated by the 1996 Telecoms Act, it said.

Total revenues from new products and services rose nearly 50 percent from a year earlier to about $232 million in the first quarter. Total vertical services revenue of about $266 million was up 21 percent. Vertical services are value-added features beyond basic access, such as Caller ID and voice messaging.
U S West said it had added 688,000 access lines, adjusted for the sales of rural exchanges, over the past 12 months, for an access line growth rate of 4.6 percent.
On an adjusted basis, business access lines grew at 6.3 percent, while residential access lines grew at 3.9 percent.
It said it had a 29 percent increase in residential customer additional access lines versus the 1996 first quarter, boosting total penetration of the service to 11.6 percent of its customers.

It said Caller ID subscribers rose by an unprecendented 900,000 in the first quarter due to an aggressive promotional campaign, driving residential penetration of the new product to 26 percent of its customers. It said revenues from these sales will largely begin during the second quarter.
Voice messaging subscriber levels reached over 1.3 million, driving residential penetration of this product to about 16 percent, the company said.

U S West said it had a 9.2 percent rise in total access revenues, to almost $900 million, for the first quarter, on accelerating dedicated access sales, continued growth in switched access minutes of use, and solid access line growth.
Data networking services revenues rose to more than $67 million, up 63 percent from the 1996 first quarter.

"U S West Communications Group has started off 1997 with double-digit momentum on the heels of 1996's accelerating results," said Richard McCormick, chairman and chief executive of U S West Inc, the holding group for the phone company.
"The U S West Communications team has struck the delicate balance of running the business for today while building it for tomorrow," he said.

"This quarter's strong results reflect continued cost-control initiatives, the step-up of marketing efforts, and the continued vitality of our operating territory," said U S West Communications President and CEO Sol Trujillo.
It was the third consecutive quarter in which employee-related and total operating expense growth slowed. Employee costs fell 0.9 percent to $806 million, U S West said.

It said the growth in operating costs was largely attributable to a step-up in marketing activity associated with Caller ID and brand enhancement campaigns. Operating margins rose to 24.9 percent from 24.2 percent year-over-year.
U S West Communications Group provides telecommunications and high-speed data networking services to more than 25 million customers in 14 western and midwestern states.
The company is one of two major groups that make up U S West Inc. The other is U S West Media Group, a supplier of cable service operators.
U S West Communications shares rose one to 32-3/8 in trading Friday morning.
((--Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1736))
